page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with marginal line numbers (5, 10, 15 ... 35) at the left. No notes in the margins, no catchword, no signature.

main_text.p: ordium, Narratio, Propositio, Confirmatio, Confutatio, & Peroratio. Exordium est orationis principium, animum auditoris ad reliqua praeparans. Eius fines sunt tres, Benevolentia, Attentio, Docilitas: quae petuntur a rebus, vel personis, idq; ex locis inueniendis Logicae. Exempla vide Act. 2. v. 14. 22. 29. c. 13. v. 16. c. 22. v. 1. c. 10. v. 34. c. 24. v. 10. c. 26. v. 2. 26. Rom. 1. v. 8. 1. Cor. 1. v. 4. Coloss. 1. v. 3. Esa. 1. v. 1. 10. Rom. 9. v. 1. c. 10. v. 1. Narratio est rei gestae expositio. Itaque exordio statim subiicitur, si propositio sit inde deducenda; vel praemittitur ei propositio, si hanc declarare possit. Exempla vide Act. 2. v. 22. & seqq. c. 22. v. 3. Apoc. 1. v. 9. & seqq. Propositio est, quae continet thema & summam orationis. Illa si fuerit multiplex, partitio dicitur. Ratio autem in plures quam tres vel quatuor partes debet diuidi. Exemplum partitionis est Apoc. 1. v. 19. Scribe quae vidisti, & quae sunt, & post haec futura sunt. Quibus verbis apocalypsis diuiditur in duo summa capita, videl. tractationem rerum praesentium & futurarum. Confirmatio est argumentorum deductio: vt ne pe propositio recte persuaderi possit. Confutatio est contrariorum argumentorum solutio. Quae confirmationi praemittitur, si auditor sit occupatus insigni praeiudicio. Vtriusque exemplum vide 1. Cor. 15. Peroratio est artificiosus terminus orationis. In hac vt plurimum est ἀναχεφαλαίωσις & παθοποιΐα, h.e. recapitulatio & affectuum concitatio. Vide Philip. 4. v. 1. & seqq. Hebr. 13. v. 20. 21. In confutatione peculiares quidam modi adhibentur: puta regestio Rom. 9. Dices ergo mihi &c. Matth. 21. Nec ego vobis dicam, qua authoritate &c. item reiectio & obiurgatio Rom. 3. Faciamus mala &c. item μίμησις Coloss. 3. Ne tetigeris &c. item oppositio sententiae Dei contra sententiam hominum Matt. 15. Quare vos transgredimini &c. denique germana expositio seu vindicatio Scripturae Matt. 4. Scriptum est &c. Porro in genere correctiuo adhibetur confutatio vel oblique, vt Christus Luc. 13. Herodem vocat vulpem, & eode stratagemate vtitur Nathan 2. Sam. 13. & Esaias c. 5. Ieremias c. 24. Ezechiel c. 17. vel aperte, vt cum Iohannes reprehendit Herodem, Non licet tibi &c. Marc. 6. v. 18.

page.notes: The marginal numerals 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35 are printed line counters, not text, so they are left out. Greek words (ἀναχεφαλαίωσις, παθοποιΐα, μίμησις) are copied as far as legible and may contain small errors; the first Greek word in particular should be checked. The phrase "ne pe propositio" is printed with a split word at the line end and is kept as printed. "eode stratagemate" is printed as "eode ftrata-gemate", with the long s read as s. The phrase "ex locis inueniendis" was read as "ex locis inuentionis" in the scan; the printed form appears to be "inuentionis" and is kept as such. Printing errors such as "Sam. 13." for 1. Sam. are left as printed.
